caveats: The conversion measures are aggregate historical diagnostics. Lead/win and enquiry/seat cohorts are not matched; forecast lags are explicit assumptions.
Spend covers both corporate and open activities. A whole-funnel proportional-spend model can scale both historical outputs together, but is not a measured channel-specific CAC or causal elasticity.
Do not add marketing-supported wins on top of an unchanged total salesperson forecast: they are a route to the same customer revenue, not a separate revenue line.
Historical 58 wins and 49 delivered corporate programs measure different stages. Do not assume that every recorded win was delivered in the same month.
Sales director says approximately one quarter of corporate growth, not one quarter of all corporate revenue, comes from marketing enquiries.

part1DemandModel.method: Keep existing 2026 spend and activity mix. Estimate enquiries/leads using corresponding 2025 month volumes multiplied by the 2026/2025 monthly spend ratio. Apply pooled historical conversion with an explicit lag. This is a conservative planning assumption, not a proved demand curve.
part1DemandModel.openFormula: 2026 marketing enquiries[m] = 2025 enquiries[m] * 2026 spend[m] / 2025 spend[m]. Potential delivered seats[m] = enquiries[m-1] * (198/817). Integer seats = ROUNDDOWN(potential seats,0). Actual served seats require a scheduled event and cannot exceed 20 per existing room/date.
part1DemandModel.timingSource: 03 Sales Director Plan.docx ¶11 (open seats usually sell in four weeks before an event); 05 Operations and Trainer Plan.docx ¶14,¶19

januaryCarryover.meaning: Use the observed December 2025 enquiry count as an explicit opening-pipeline proxy. It is not a signed order or a guarantee that all enquiries remain live.
januaryCarryover.source: 02 Historical Results and Draft P&L Budget.xlsx / 03 Prior Year Marketing!O11; 04 Marketing Director Plan.docx ¶8

part1DemandModel.corporateFormula: Qualified leads generated in month m = 2025 leads[m] * 2026 spend[m] / 2025 spend[m]. Expected marketing-supported wins delivered around m+2 use historical 58/288 conversion, subject to staff/client/program capacity. Unknown January–February delivery pipeline must be stated separately; no automatic immediate revenue from autumn campaign.

interpretation: Do not impose 12 as a demand floor. Company background says a normal event can assemble about12–20 participants; insufficient enquiries can leave an event with fewer attendees.
Do not force the planned136 seats to be sold. At the existing seven dates, the explicit lagged funnel gives a lower attendance estimate; monthly program economics must use that attendance.

The adopted Part 1 forecast serves only the seven explicitly scheduled open dates. Unserved demand in other months is disclosed as potential, not booked revenue. Adding four dates is a separate management decision in Part 2.
The scheduled-seven-date result is a diagnostic, not a direction to cancel existing events or a complete company revenue forecast.

The one-month lag is approximate. Current event promotion can convert within the same month; show a no-lag alternative as a timing sensitivity rather than selectively using whichever month produces more seats.

part2Proposals.feasibility: Capture existing unserved enquiry potential in four months, without assigning the same enquiry cohort to another event. Existing planned seven dates continue in both versions. Allocate eight additional external trainer days and eight room days, price each at EUR600 per seat, and record every event in the management delivery register. Customer willingness to buy this premium offer and January lead time are explicit risks.

materialRisks: Funnel cohorts and source attribution are incomplete; no measured budget-to-demand elasticity or conversion uplift exists.
Anna client retention requires a real owner afterFebruary. Merely deleting her salary does not preserve her sales target.
Ella productivity stages are known; exact ramp percentages and client wins remain assumptions.
Autumn spending can generate delivered corporate sales late in the year or2027. December renewal messages mostly benefit next year.
A full program calendar cannot be derived from annual revenue alone. Demand and delivery constraints must be integrated before P&L revenue is recognised.

Source catalogue calls the premium open course Executive Blame Delegation; marketing refers to Professional Blame Delegation. Clarify the advertised offer and correct quoted prices without silently inventing a new course.

The submitted 2026 appropriation already includes website/testimonial/campaign activities. Do not add those as separate automatic Part1 charges without evidence, and do not make them disappear as automatic Part1 savings.
recommendation: Part 1 retains all existing monthly marketing activities and actual staffing dates. Forecast attendance only on the seven existing open dates using a one-month lag and the pooled historical conversion, without a twelve-seat floor or conversion uplift. Part 2 approves four additional dates against unserved demand and includes EUR1,000 setup plus all delivery costs. Revenue remains constrained by paying customers, advance bookings and the delivery calendar.
